name: guardian_xql_templates
description: Ready-made XQL queries for GuardianXQL: who changed a resource, who only read it, what an identity or an IP did, which permissions an identity never used, and whether a data source is still sending (its health rows, the sources behind one sender, raw and modeled event counts per hour). Each has placeholders filled from checked arguments. The model may still write raw XQL with xdr-xql-generic-query; these only make the common questions easy. Add a template here without changing any script.
data:
{
 "version": 1,
 "templates": [
  {
   "name": "identity_activity",
   "dataset": "cloud_audit_logs",
   "params": [
    "identity"
   ],
   "default_hours": 6,
   "max_hours": 72,
   "description": "What one identity did in the cloud audit log: operations, outcomes, source IPs and networks, user agents and resources, grouped by operation. Pass a user principal name (alice@example.test), an object id, or a DOMAIN\\account (matched by the account name before the @ across all domains). Use it to see the session around an alert and to spot sign-in failures, IAM changes and new source networks.",
   "query": "dataset = cloud_audit_logs | filter (lowercase(identity_name) = \"{identity_lc}\" or lowercase(identity_uuid) = \"{identity_lc}\") | comp count() as events, values(caller_ip) as ips, values(caller_ip_asn_org) as asns, values(user_agent) as agents, values(referenced_resource_name) as resources, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen by operation_name, operation_status, cloud_provider | sort desc events | limit 50",
   "account_query": "dataset = cloud_audit_logs | filter arrayindex(split(lowercase(identity_name), \"@\"), 0) = \"{account}\" | comp count() as events, values(caller_ip) as ips, values(caller_ip_asn_org) as asns, values(user_agent) as agents, values(referenced_resource_name) as resources, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen by operation_name, operation_status, cloud_provider | sort desc events | limit 50"
  },
  {
   "name": "resource_change_history",
   "dataset": "cloud_audit_logs",
   "params": [
    "resource"
   ],
   "default_hours": 72,
   "max_hours": 720,
   "description": "Who changed one cloud resource and when: state-changing operations on it, newest first, with the identity and source IP. Use it for a misconfiguration whose change was recent.",
   "query": "dataset = cloud_audit_logs | filter (lowercase(referenced_resource) = \"{resource_lc}\" or lowercase(referenced_resource_name) = \"{resource_lc}\") and state_changing_event = \"true\" | fields _time, identity_name, identity_type, operation_name, operation_status, caller_ip | sort desc _time | limit 50"
  },
  {
   "name": "resource_access_activity",
   "dataset": "cloud_audit_logs",
   "params": [
    "resource"
   ],
   "default_hours": 24,
   "max_hours": 168,
   "description": "Who read or used one cloud resource without changing it: identity, type, operations, source IPs and when, most active first. Use it to see who touched a storage account, key or database that is exposed or was changed.",
   "query": "dataset = cloud_audit_logs | filter (lowercase(referenced_resource) = \"{resource_lc}\" or lowercase(referenced_resource_name) = \"{resource_lc}\") and (state_changing_event = \"false\" or state_changing_event = null) | comp count() as events, values(operation_name) as operations, values(caller_ip) as ips, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen by identity_name, identity_type | sort desc events | limit 50"
  },
  {
   "name": "ip_activity",
   "dataset": "cloud_audit_logs",
   "params": [
    "ip"
   ],
   "default_hours": 24,
   "max_hours": 168,
   "description": "What one source IP did in the cloud audit log: which identities used it and which operations they ran, with the network owner and country. Use it to judge whether an address is routine for this environment.",
   "query": "dataset = cloud_audit_logs | filter caller_ip = \"{ip}\" | comp count() as events, values(caller_ip_asn_org) as asns, values(caller_ip_geolocation) as geo, values(user_agent) as agents, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen by identity_name, operation_name | sort desc events | limit 50"
  },
  {
   "name": "identity_unused_permissions",
   "dataset": "ciem_permissions_with_last_access",
   "params": [
    "identity"
   ],
   "default_hours": 24,
   "max_hours": 24,
   "description": "The permissions one identity or compute resource holds, one row each: the action, its access level, whether it is administrative, the resource and service it applies to, the policy that grants it, and last_access_time. An empty last_access_time means never used, unless is_last_access_supported is false, in which case the platform does not track access for that permission.",
   "query": "dataset = ciem_permissions_with_last_access | filter source_cloud_resource_name contains \"{identity}\" | fields source_cloud_resource_name, source_cloud_resource_type, action_name, action_access_level, action_access_isadministrative, dest_cloud_resource_name, dest_cloud_service_name, grantedby_cloud_policy_name, is_last_access_supported, last_access_time | limit 100"
  },
  {
   "name": "source_ingestion_health",
   "dataset": "metrics_view",
   "params": [
    "vendor",
    "product"
   ],
   "default_hours": 24,
   "max_hours": 168,
   "description": "Is one data source still sending, and through what: events in the window, when it was last seen, its collector types, the devices that report it and the brokers it goes through, from the data source health rows. Pass the vendor and product as the platform lists them (case does not matter). No row, or an old last_seen, means the source is silent. Read `last_seen_utc` (the last event, already in UTC), `hours_silent` (hours since then) and `state` (`stopped` after more than 2 silent hours, else `flowing`); never convert the raw `last_seen` number yourself; `max_delay` is the platform's `data_freshness_max_delay` in the units of the health rows; `events` is the sum of `total_event_count` in the window.",
   "query": "preset = metrics_view | filter lowercase(_vendor) = \"{vendor_lc}\" and lowercase(_product) = \"{product_lc}\" | comp sum(total_event_count) as events, max(last_seen) as last_seen, max(data_freshness_max_delay) as max_delay, values(_collector_type) as collectors, values(_reporting_device_ip) as reporters, values(_broker_device_name) as brokers by _vendor, _product | alter last_seen_utc = format_timestamp(\"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC\", last_seen), hours_silent = timestamp_diff(current_time(), last_seen, \"HOUR\") | alter state = if(hours_silent > 2, \"stopped\", \"flowing\")"
  },
  {
   "name": "reporter_sources",
   "dataset": "metrics_view",
   "params": [
    "ip"
   ],
   "default_hours": 24,
   "max_hours": 168,
   "description": "Every data source that arrives through one sending device (as the reporting device, the final reporting device or the broker), oldest last_seen first. Use it to tell whether all sources behind one sender stopped together (the sender, a relay or the network path) or only one (that product's own export). Read `last_seen_utc` (the last event, already in UTC), `hours_silent` (hours since then) and `state` (`stopped` after more than 2 silent hours, else `flowing`); never convert the raw `last_seen` number yourself; `max_delay` is the platform's `data_freshness_max_delay` in the units of the health rows; `events` is the sum of `total_event_count` in the window. Sources whose `last_seen_utc` falls in the same few minutes stopped together and share a cause: count them.",
   "query": "preset = metrics_view | filter _reporting_device_ip = \"{ip}\" or _final_reporting_device_ip = \"{ip}\" or _broker_device_ip = \"{ip}\" | comp sum(total_event_count) as events, max(last_seen) as last_seen, max(data_freshness_max_delay) as max_delay, values(_reporting_device_ip) as reporters, values(_broker_device_name) as brokers by _vendor, _product, _collector_type | alter last_seen_utc = format_timestamp(\"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC\", last_seen), hours_silent = timestamp_diff(current_time(), last_seen, \"HOUR\") | alter state = if(hours_silent > 2, \"stopped\", \"flowing\") | sort asc last_seen"
  },
  {
   "name": "dataset_raw_volume",
   "dataset": "{dataset}",
   "params": [
    "dataset"
   ],
   "default_hours": 24,
   "max_hours": 72,
   "description": "Raw events per hour of one dataset (pass its name, lowercase). Compare with datamodel_volume: raw events with no modeled events mean no modeling rule is bound to the dataset or its filter does not match; no raw events mean the source is silent. The `_time` of each row is the start of the hour.",
   "query": "dataset = {dataset} | bin _time span = 1h | comp count() as raw_events by _time | sort asc _time"
  },
  {
   "name": "datamodel_volume",
   "dataset": "{dataset}",
   "params": [
    "dataset"
   ],
   "default_hours": 24,
   "max_hours": 72,
   "description": "Modeled events per hour of one dataset, counted in the data model (pass the raw dataset's name, lowercase). Fewer modeled than raw events per hour is a parsing or modeling-rule yield problem. The `_time` of each row is the start of the hour.",
   "query": "datamodel dataset = {dataset} | bin _time span = 1h | comp count() as modeled_events by _time | sort asc _time"
  }
 ]
}
